newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Novartis regrets French ban on gene-corn.
newsitem.headline: Novartis regrets French ban on gene-corn.

text.p: Pharma giant Novartis AG, the merged successor to Swiss groups Ciba-Geigy and Sandoz, said a French ban on planting genetically altered corn gave that country's farmers a competitive disadvantage.

Novartis said it hoped the French government would change its mind and allow farmers to plant the corn, which was developed by Ciba to resist the corn borer pest. It has been approved for planting by the EU, United States and Canada.
"It is unfortunate for the farmers," the spokesman said about the French decision on Wednesday to bar cultivation of the so-called Bt-maize.
"This decision effectively takes a tool out of the farmers' hands and gives them a competitive disadvantage," a Novartis spokesman told Reuters.
"Corn borer is a big problem here in Europe...especially in France, Spain and Italy," the spokesman added, saying up to 20 percent of a harvest could be lost to the pest.
France this week authorised the import and marketing of genetically altered corn but refused to allow its planting, saying the government wanted to move step by step.
